newsitem.title: UK: EU says no new criteria after first wave of EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU says no new criteria after first wave of EMU.

text.p: European Union monetary affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday that countries joining EMU after the first wave would not have to adopt new policies "cooked up between the ins".
Speaking to a branch of the "1992 club' in southern England, De Silguy said there was no question of changing the Treaty provisions for EMU or the criteria for participation.
"Countries that want to join after January 1 1999, will not be obliged to adopt a range of new policies cooked up between the ins," he said.
De Silguy reiterated that economic convergence and practical preparations towards European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) were firmly on track.
"The average deficit in the Union has fallen from 5.4 percent of GDP in 1994 to 4.4 pct in 1996. The goal is within reach," he said.
He also said the introduction of a single currency would not need harmonisation of tax and social security systems.
